title: TikTok gut health advice: Is it reliable for IBS? | Nerva
summary: A Tufts study found the least accurate gut health advice on TikTok gets the most likes. Learn how to spot credible IBS advice and what actually helps.
body_markdown:
IBS is a gut-brain disorder, meaning the gut and brain communicate in a way that makes the gut more sensitive.


That’s why the American College of Gastroenterology, which sets the IBS treatment guidelines US doctors follow, and the Rome Foundation, the international group of experts that defines how gut-brain disorders are diagnosed, both recommend therapies like gut-directed hypnotherapy alongside diet and medication.⁴ ⁵ These therapies work by targeting the gut-brain signaling behind symptoms.


## Is Nerva evidence-based?


Nerva is an evidence-based gut-brain therapy program, tested in a randomized controlled trial where 81% of people achieved a clinically meaningful improvement in IBS symptoms.⁶


It was developed with Dr. Simone Peters, a co-creator of Nerva, whose Monash University research found gut-directed hypnotherapy worked as well as the low FODMAP diet for IBS.⁷


Unlike the latest GutTok trend, Nerva won’t ask you to cleanse, cut out foods, or buy another supplement. Instead, it works alongside your existing medical care to help calm the gut-brain signaling behind your symptoms. Every part of the program is built on clinical trials, not likes, so you can trust it’s been tested in people like you before it ever reached your phone.


## Frequently asked questions


### What is GutTok?


GutTok is the nickname for gut health content on TikTok, from bloating hacks to supplement reviews. It can help people feel less alone with digestive symptoms, but the quality of advice varies widely.


### Should I tell my doctor about gut health advice I found online?


Telling your doctor about advice you’ve found online helps them understand what you’ve already tried and spot anything that could be affecting your symptoms. Gastroenterologists and dietitians expect these conversations, so there’s no need to feel embarrassed.


### Can stress make IBS symptoms worse?


Stress can make IBS symptoms worse because the gut and brain are in constant two-way communication. Many people notice flare-ups during busy or stressful periods, even when their diet hasn’t changed.


### Is gut-directed hypnotherapy the same as regular hypnosis?


Gut-directed hypnotherapy is different from stage hypnosis – it uses guided relaxation and gut-focused suggestions to calm gut-brain signaling, and you stay in control the whole time. Gut-brain therapy programs like Nerva deliver it in short daily sessions you can do at home.
